pages.text: Splash, splash! The wheel made its first turn. Spray tapped the round window. Little brother Mumu shook the covers. "Dodo, the wheel is turning! Morning!" Big sister Dodo pulled her covers over her head. "Five more minutes..."

"I know. The wheel turns without me." Dodo shut her eyes tight. Dad from the mill called from the door, "Dodo, I opened the sluice gate, the door holding back stream water. We're baking the first bread!" Dodo still slept.
Much later, Dodo woke with a start. The sun filled the round window. Bread smelled delicious downstairs. "The wheel turns without me. But bread doesn't wait!" Dodo shuffled her feet.
Dad came up and sat beside Dodo. "When the gate opens, stretch your body long. That chases sleep away." He reached both wings up high. Dodo stretched her long wings too.
Wings stretch! Long legs stretch! Neck stretch! Oh? Dodo became the longest in the room. "Stretching sends sleep away!" Her eyes sparkled, wide awake.
"Open the window and greet the wheel?" Dad said behind her. Dodo opened it wide. Spray tapped her face. Cool! "Hello, waterwheel! Sluice gate opens—stretch, stretch!" she called.
Downstairs by the water jar, Dodo bent her neck low and splashed her face with both wings. Droplets tapped the jar rim. "Clean! All done!" One flick of her tail.
At the table, the first bread was already gone. Only one piece remained on Mumu's plate. He tore his bread in half and offered it. "I saved yours!" Dodo ate. "After stretching, it tastes better!"
Now Dodo knew the morning order. "One, gate opens, stretch long! Two, open the window, greet the wheel! Three, wash my face clean!" The next day, she came down before Dad called.
Dad hugged Dodo against his broad chest. "Up and lively, like the wheel!" Stretch long, and sleep slips away. Dodo lifted her chin. "Sluice gate opens—stretch, stretch!"
